topics.label: Lecture introduction and objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the final lecture and outlines its core learning objectives regarding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional modalities for treating tumors, including surgical resection, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapeutic agents along with their mechanisms and toxicities.

topics.label: Exploiting molecular and genetic vulnerabilities of cancer cells
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic approaches that exploit intrinsic cancer cell defects, including hormone dependency, checkpoint deficiencies, and DNA repair alterations.

topics.label: Targeting oncogenic kinases and managing drug resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the design and clinical application of small-molecule kinase inhibitors targeting oncogene addiction, alongside the molecular mechanisms of resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Antibody-based therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how engineered monoclonal antibodies and cytotoxic antibody-drug conjugates target tumor surface antigens to eliminate cancer cells.

topics.label: Cancer immune surveillance and cellular immunotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biological basis of tumor immune surveillance and clinical immunotherapies, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific antibodies, and CAR T-cell therapies.

topics.label: Challenges, historical trends, and future perspectives in cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine overarching clinical challenges, historical survival trends, genomic profiling, and ethical dilemmas shaping modern cancer management.
